name: Azure Virtual Machines
tagline: On-demand, scalable IaaS compute with full OS control.
whatItIs: Windows and Linux virtual machines in hundreds of sizes, with managed disks, virtual networking and availability options.
primaryPurpose: Run workloads that need full control over the operating system.
keyFeatures: Size families (B, D, E, F, L, M, N, H)
security: Avoid public IPs; use Bastion or JIT
Encrypt disks with platform or customer-managed keys
networking: Each VM has at least one NIC in a subnet; NSGs on NIC/subnet; optional Standard public IP
pricing: Per second of compute while allocated (by size/OS license), plus disks, networking and any licenses. Reservations, savings plans and Spot reduce cost.

confusedWith.name: App Service
confusedWith.difference: PaaS for web apps with no OS management.

confusedWith.name: Container Instances
confusedWith.difference: Runs containers without a VM to manage.

relevanceNote: Creating, sizing, encrypting, moving and making VMs highly available are core skills.
examTips: Availability options are chosen at creation

name: Virtual Machine Scale Sets
whatItIs: Manage and scale a group of VMs from one configuration, in Flexible or Uniform orchestration mode.
security: Same as VMs — use managed identities, Bastion, patching
networking: Integrates with Load Balancer and Application Gateway backend pools
pricing: No extra charge; pay for the VMs, disks and networking used.

confusedWith.name: Availability sets
confusedWith.difference: Static placement of individual VMs; no autoscale.

relevanceNote: Deploying and configuring scale sets is an explicit skill.
examTips: Orchestration mode can't be changed later

docLinks.title: What are Virtual Machine Scale Sets?

name: Azure Managed Disks
whatItIs: Durable block storage managed by Azure, in Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk types.
primaryPurpose: Persistent OS and data disks for VMs.
keyFeatures: Server-side encryption with PMK or CMK (disk encryption sets)
security: Encryption at rest always on; CMK via disk encryption sets
Restrict export with private links for disk access (Disk Access)
networking: Disk export/import can be restricted to private endpoints via Disk Access resources
pricing: By provisioned size and type (and performance for Premium SSD v2/Ultra), plus snapshots and transactions for some tiers.

confusedWith.name: Temporary disk
confusedWith.difference: The temp disk is local, non-persistent host storage — not a managed disk.

relevanceNote: Managing VM disks is in the outline.
examTips: Ultra/Premium SSD v2 can't be OS disks

name: Azure Compute Gallery
tagline: Share and replicate VM images and applications.
whatItIs: A repository (formerly Shared Image Gallery) for image definitions and versions and VM applications, with regional replication and sharing.
useCases: Sharing images with other subscriptions or tenants
Deploying scale sets from custom images
keyFeatures: Replication to multiple regions with replica counts
Sharing via RBAC, direct shared gallery or community gallery
security: Generalize images to remove machine-specific data
pricing: No gallery charge; pay for image storage and replication egress.

confusedWith.name: Managed image
confusedWith.difference: A single-region image resource without versioning or replication.

relevanceNote: Appears in VM deployment and image-management scenarios.
examTips: Use the gallery to share images across subscriptions/regions

name: ARM Templates & Bicep
tagline: Native infrastructure as code for Azure.
whatItIs: Declarative JSON templates and the Bicep language that compiles to them, deployed through Azure Resource Manager.
security: Use secure parameters and Key Vault references
Deployment history can expose parameter values — avoid plain-text secrets

confusedWith.name: Terraform
confusedWith.difference: Third-party IaC with a state file; ARM/Bicep are Azure-native and stateless.

relevanceNote: Interpreting, modifying and deploying templates/Bicep is a full objective.
examTips: Complete mode deletes unlisted resources in the RG
'az bicep decompile' converts JSON to Bicep

name: Azure App Service
tagline: Managed hosting for web apps and APIs.
whatItIs: A PaaS for web applications, REST APIs and containers, running on App Service plans with built-in scaling, deployment slots and security features.
primaryPurpose: Run web apps without managing infrastructure.
networking: Outbound: VNet integration. Inbound private: private endpoints. Access restrictions for public inbound.
pricing: Per App Service plan instance by tier and size; Free/Shared tiers for dev/test.

confusedWith.name: Azure Functions
confusedWith.difference: Event-driven serverless code; App Service hosts full web apps (Functions can run on App Service plans).

relevanceNote: An entire objective covers App Service plans, scaling, TLS, domains, backup, networking and slots.
examTips: Custom domain needs a TXT asuid record

name: Azure Container Registry
whatItIs: A managed, private Docker/OCI registry with build tasks, geo-replication and security integrations.
primaryPurpose: Store and distribute container images close to deployments.
useCases: Images for ACI, ACA, App Service and AKS
security: Use Entra identities/managed identities with AcrPull; keep admin user disabled
networking: Public endpoint with firewall rules or private endpoints (Premium)
pricing: Daily rate by SKU plus storage beyond included and data transfer.

confusedWith.name: Docker Hub
confusedWith.difference: Public registry service; ACR is private and Azure-integrated.

relevanceNote: Creating and managing a container registry is listed.

name: Azure Container Instances
tagline: Run containers on demand without servers.
whatItIs: Serverless containers billed per second, deployed as container groups with set CPU and memory.
primaryPurpose: The simplest way to run a container in Azure.
keyFeatures: Public IP/DNS label or VNet deployment
networking: Public IP with DNS name label, or deploy into a VNet subnet
pricing: Per second for requested vCPU and memory (and GPU where used).

confusedWith.name: Container Apps
confusedWith.difference: ACA adds autoscaling, revisions and ingress for microservices.

relevanceNote: Provisioning containers with ACI and managing sizing are listed.

name: Azure Container Apps
tagline: Serverless containers with autoscaling and microservice features.
whatItIs: A managed platform for containerized apps and jobs, built on Kubernetes, KEDA, Dapr and Envoy, without cluster management.
primaryPurpose: Run scalable microservices and event-driven workloads.
useCases: Background processors scaling on queue length
keyFeatures: Scale rules (HTTP, CPU/memory, KEDA) including scale to zero
networking: Environment can be deployed into a custom VNet; external or internal ingress
pricing: Consumption billing per vCPU-second/GiB-second and requests, or dedicated workload profiles.

confusedWith.name: AKS
confusedWith.difference: AKS exposes full Kubernetes; ACA abstracts it away.

relevanceNote: Provisioning and scaling Container Apps is in the outline.
